newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FOCUS-Australia's Optus Vision CEO steps down.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FOCUS-Australia's Optus Vision CEO steps down.

text.p: The chief executive of Australian pay television operator Optus Vision, Geoffrey Cousins, announced on Thursday he would step down as chief executive and would soon take up the company's chairmanship.

He said he was stepping down as planned after Optus Vision's first year of operations, confident it had won the battle with Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd for supremacy in the cable television market.
"As far as the major strategic battles are concerned they're over and as a pay television operator Optus Vision is absolutely in the winning position," Cousins told a news conference.
He announced that Optus Vision had in excess of 100,000 customers, as measured in an independent report by KPMG Peat Marwick.
Optus Vision's only cable television competitor is Foxtel, a joint venture owned by News Corp and state-owned telecommuniciations giant Telstra Corp.
Foxtel's said earlier this week it had about 115,000 subscribers. Its cables pass by well over a million homes.
Microwave and satellite pay television operator Australis Media Ltd said last week it had 108,000 subscribers.
Cousins said Optus Vision's cables had passed over a million homes, although many were not yet able to access the cables, so Optus' penetration rate was better than Foxtel's.
"If you look at the figures we've released, the penetration of Optus Vision is substantially ahead of its competitors," Cousins said.
He said Optus Vision would be adding five new pay television channels by the end of January 1997 -- the Warner movie Channel, one Arabic Channel, one Italian Channel and two Greek Channels.
Optus Vision had also just signed a long-term exclusive programming supply deal with filmmaker Steven Spielberg's DreamWorks SKG movie production house.
He said Optus Visions alliances with the Warner Group, the Disney Organisation and Channels seven and nine in Australia showed it had won the strategic battle for programming.
Cousins said Optus Vision was satisfied with its current churn rates.
Pay television operators refer to the loss of subscribers and the signing on of new subscribers as "churning".
"For us we're very satisfied with the churn rates and they're coming down and we'd expect them to come down much further once we've got many more telephony customers on board," he said.

Optus Vision is 46.5 percent owned by both Australian telecommunications carrier Optus Communications and Continental CableVision Inc, which has merged with U.S. West. The balance of Optus Vision is owned by Seven Network Ltd and Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd.
Cousins said Optus Vision hoped to find a replacement within weeks or a couple of months at most, but that it would not look overseas for his replacement as chief executive.

"I'm not a great fan of this trend of hiring chief executives for Australian firms from overseas. I don't understand that trend and I don't think it's a healthy one," he said. "We won't be looking at any overseas candidates."
Foxtel and Telstra are both headed by Americans.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
